content:
Apple shares fell significantly after the keynote at the Worldwide Developers Conference, and some analysts attributed this to market disappointment with the company's artificial intelligence announcements.

While we don't entirely agree with that analysis, investors now seem to quite welcome the company's prudent stance on AI spending, and the share price has rebounded 15% from its June low...

The share price fell 4% the day after the keynote, although multiple macroeconomic factors were weighing on stocks at the time, including US military strikes against Iran after one of its helicopters was shot down.

The share price subsequently rebounded more strongly, once again approaching record highs. Bloomberg pointed to artificial intelligence as one of the factors, albeit with a more indirect impact. The outlet noted that investors are increasingly focusing on AI spending at other companies, while Apple's relatively cautious approach is now being seen as an advantage.

Apple's share price reversal reflects growing market concerns over whether massive artificial intelligence spending will deliver returns. Although the company's own AI products have repeatedly disappointed investors, Apple's decision not to join the data centre arms race is increasingly being viewed as an asset rather than a liability. Mark Bronzo, Chief Investment Strategist at Rye Strategic Partners, said: 'The market is in a tug-of-war, and Apple is benefiting for now because it's not at the centre of the AI deal vortex. People are worried about what returns the hyperscale cloud providers will get from AI spending...'

Analysts reportedly aren't worried that the company's price hikes will dent demand, and have welcomed its decision to defend margins. JPMorgan said past price increases have not materially impacted demand, and expressed optimism about the potential revenue from a possible iPhone Ultra launch.

While this may be overly optimistic, there does appear to be broad consensus in the market that Apple's financials are heading in the right direction, with net income expected to grow 17% this fiscal year.
